newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia wool pile falls below two mln bales.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia wool pile falls below two mln bales.

text.p: Australia's wool stockpile had fallen below two million bales, Wool Council of Australia president Rod Thirkell-Johnston said on Wednesday.
The outstanding debt of Wool International (WI) also had been reduced to an estimated A$900 million at the end of November, he said in a statement.

Significant buying interest for the last 20,000 bales for December delivery had also resulted in the completion of December quarter sales. March quarter forward sales totalled about 10,000 bales, he said.
"This solid progress is good news for woolgrowers who have been subjected to sustained low prices. As the stockpile is further run down growers can expect a more positive market outlook," he said.

It was welcome that the remaining two million bales could be sold with greater flexibility and therefore with a reduced impact on the fresh wool market because of a bill now waiting debate in the Australian Senate requiring WI to sell a minimum 135,000 bales in the coming March and June quarters, he said.
Australia's wool stockpile, which peaked at 4.72 million bales in 1991, would be down to about 1.7 million bales by June 1997, Thirkell-Johnston said.
The debt peaked at A$2.8 billion in 1991.
